I have created an illustration of the moment from Deuteronomy 1:7, rendered as an early Renaissance fresco with the matte, chalky texture of paint on plaster. The scene depicts the Israelite people breaking camp at the base of Mount Horeb (as described in the setting and reference) and beginning to turn and journey toward the hill country. 

In the foreground, Moses stands on a rocky rise, gesturing with an outstretched arm toward the path ahead, holding his wooden staff. Beside him, Joshua is shown watching over the community. The large assembly of Israelites—men, women, and children with warm, weathered features—are busy packing supplies, loading donkeys and oxen, and beginning to march forward to the right. The dark, steep peak of Mount Horeb, wrapped in natural clouds, rises in the background on the left, with the dry desert plains and hills extending into the distance under an even, pale lapis sky. No modern features, text, or border are included, ensuring it retains the look of a continuous narrative fresco.
